Native depletion compromises aconitase maturation and becomes lethal under elevated oxygen, while its precise chemical contribution remains unresolved. This IscA is distinct from the NifIscA paralog encoded in the nitrogen-fixation region.

genes/ECOLI/fdx/fdx-ai-review.yaml.description: Fdx is a small (111-residue) cytosolic [2Fe-2S] ferredoxin of the adrenodoxin/putidaredoxin family, encoded as the last structural gene of the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. Its single [2Fe-2S] cluster is ligated by four cysteines, and the cluster can itself be supplied by the Isc system (for example from holo-IscA). Fdx acts as a one-electron carrier for Fe-S cluster biogenesis: it binds the cysteine desulfurase IscS near the active-site Cys328 loop, on a surface that overlaps the binding sites of IscU and the frataxin CyaY, and reduced Fdx donates an electron to the IscS persulfide formed during cysteine turnover, a step needed for [2Fe-2S] cluster formation on IscU. Loss of fdx causes Fe-S enzyme defects similar to those of iscU, hscB and hscA mutants. An E. coli NADPH–ferredoxin-NADP reductase (FNR/Fpr P28861)–Fdx chain sustains IscS/IscU cluster formation in vitro. This establishes a compatible reductant supply without proving exclusive donor usage or flux under every native growth condition.

genes/ECOLI/hscA/hscA-ai-review.yaml.description: HscA (Hsc66) is a specialized cytosolic Hsp70-family chaperone encoded with its J-type co-chaperone HscB in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It has a low intrinsic ATPase activity, limited by ATP hydrolysis rather than nucleotide exchange, and needs no GrpE-type exchange factor. Its substrate-binding domain recognizes a conserved LPPVK loop of the Fe-S scaffold protein IscU, and HscB delivers IscU to the ATP-bound state of HscA; together IscU and HscB stimulate HscA ATP hydrolysis about 500-fold, trapping IscU in the ADP-bound complex. ATP hydrolysis by the 1:1:1 HscA-HscB-IscU[2Fe-2S] complex distorts the IscU-bound cluster and accelerates [2Fe-2S] cluster transfer to acceptor apoproteins such as ferredoxin, so HscA acts as the ATP-driven engine of cluster release in Isc-mediated Fe-S protein maturation. HscA also binds cluster-deficient biotin synthase and improves its in vivo [2Fe-2S] cluster assembly, and its expression is induced by cold shock. Direct conformational measurements show preferential stabilization of disordered IscU, consistent with a holdase-like mechanism; a general folding or refolding role is not established by these cluster-transfer experiments.

genes/ECOLI/iscA/iscA-ai-review.yaml.description: IscA is a small (107-residue) cytosolic A-type iron-sulfur cluster carrier protein of the HesB/IscA family, encoded in the E. coli iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx-iscX operon. It forms dimers and tetramers whose three invariant cysteines (Cys35, Cys99, Cys101) bind either mononuclear iron or a [2Fe-2S] cluster bridged between subunits. Purified IscA binds iron with very high affinity and can donate it for IscS-dependent cluster assembly on the scaffold IscU when free iron is limiting; in cells it is iron-loaded under aerobic growth, where oxygen promotes iron binding. IscA can also assemble a [2Fe-2S] cluster and transfer it, over multiple turnovers, to apo-ferredoxin, with which holo-IscA forms a specific complex. Genetically IscA is partially redundant with its SufA paralogue (and the A-type carrier ErpA); the iscA/sufA pair is needed for Fe-S cluster assembly under aerobic but not anaerobic growth. Copper binds IscA and blocks cluster biogenesis under anaerobic copper stress. Both direct iron donation and cluster transfer are experimentally supported biochemical capabilities; their relative contribution in native cells depends on conditions and recipient proteins and does not establish IscA as the unique iron supplier to IscU.

genes/ECOLI/iscS/iscS-ai-review.yaml.description: IscS is the housekeeping pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent cysteine desulfurase of Escherichia coli, a cytosolic homodimer encoded in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It converts L-cysteine to L-alanine and carries the released sulfane sulfur as a persulfide on its active-site Cys328, located on a flexible surface loop. From this persulfide IscS delivers sulfur to a range of acceptor proteins that bind one at a time around Cys328: the scaffold IscU for assembly of [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] clusters (with frataxin/CyaY, IscX and ferredoxin acting as modulators of the IscS-IscU complex); ThiI for 4-thiouridine formation in tRNA and for thiazole/thiamine biosynthesis; TusA, the entry point of the Tus relay that leads to MnmA-catalysed 2-thiolation of the wobble uridine; and FdhD for maturation of molybdenum formate dehydrogenases. IscS also degrades L-selenocysteine in vitro and has been implicated in selenium delivery for selenophosphate synthesis. Loss of IscS abolishes tRNA s4U and causes thiamine and nicotinic acid auxotrophy and slow growth.

genes/ECOLI/iscU/iscU-ai-review.yaml.description: IscU is the small cytosolic scaffold of the E. coli Isc iron-sulfur cluster assembly machinery. It docks onto IscS, accepts persulfide sulfur through conserved cysteines, binds ferrous iron under reconstitution conditions, and assembles transient clusters. Native mass spectrometry supports both iron-loaded and sulfur-loaded intermediates; the obligatory physiological order and principal native iron-delivery route remain unresolved. Purified IscU carries [2Fe-2S] clusters and can form [4Fe-4S] clusters under reductive assembly conditions. Its structured and dynamically disordered conformations are recognized differently by IscS, HscB and HscA. HscB targets cluster-loaded IscU to HscA, whose ATPase cycle promotes cluster transfer to acceptor proteins. IscU performs repeated cluster-transfer cycles in vitro and supports maturation of defined native clients, including the Fur iron regulator. Zinc stabilizes the scaffold but can inhibit iron loading, and copper can disrupt its assembly chemistry.

suggested_experiments.description: In vivo crosslinking/pull-down of holo-IscU under HscA ATPase-dead conditions combined with acceptor proteomics to define the set of apo-proteins receiving clusters directly from IscU.

interpro/panther/PTHR10093/PTHR10093-rev.summary: The family contains U-type proteins involved in iron-sulfur protein maturation. Bacterial IscU, the N-terminal scaffold domain of NifU and eukaryotic ISU/ISCU assemble and deliver transient clusters. The Bacillus subtilis SufU member O32163 instead has strong biochemical and genetic support for zinc-dependent sulfur transfer from SufS toward the SufBCD assembly machinery, alongside earlier reports of in vitro cluster reconstitution and delivery. Similar folds therefore do not establish the same molecular activity in every member. PANTHER subfamily coverage remains incompletely resolved: E. coli IscU P0ACD4 is classified in SF8 in the PANTHER19 sequence file rather than the IscU-named SF26, and the committed inventory lacks subfamily assignments. No functionally precise subfamily boundary is inferred from names alone.
interpro/panther/PTHR10093/PTHR10093-rev.coherence_reason: Participation in Fe-S protein assembly is broadly coherent, but the molecular roles are not uniform. IscU/NifU/ISU scaffolds and zinc-dependent SufU sulfur-transfer proteins must be distinguished. E. coli IscU can bind Fe(II) in reconstituted systems, so the former bacterial-versus-eukaryotic split in free-iron binding is unsupported; differences among preparations and assembly conditions affect observed intermediates and loading order. For B. subtilis SufU, earlier positive cluster-transfer reports remain part of the evidence, while later biochemical and complementation results favor a physiological sulfur-transfer role. Neither whole-subfamily loss nor a universal cluster-delivery activity is established.

interpro/panther/PTHR19375/PTHR19375-rev.summary: The Hsp70-related family shares a nucleotide-binding domain coupled to a protein-interaction region, but includes different molecular roles. Canonical DnaK/Hsp70 proteins use nucleotide-driven client cycles for folding and related proteostasis functions. HscA is a specialized IscU-associated ATPase supporting iron-sulfur cluster transfer; direct E. coli studies show holdase and scaffold-state-selection behavior without establishing every generic folding endpoint. Hsp110 proteins provide nucleotide exchange and holdase functions for canonical Hsp70s, and other divergent members need individual assessment. Functional divergence therefore extends beyond localization. Cytosolic/nuclear, ER-lumenal and mitochondrial paralogs retain their established compartment-specific targeting and PAINT assessments; no localization conclusion is changed by this activity reconciliation.
interpro/panther/PTHR19375/PTHR19375-rev.coherence_reason: Canonical Hsp70/DnaK folding mechanisms remain strongly supported, but universal folding activity cannot be inferred from the shared fold or ATP-dependent client capture alone. HscA has directly measured ATPase, holdase and IscU-transfer functions; whether these supply the folding endpoint required by GO0140662 is unresolved for the reviewed targets. Existing Hsp110 nucleotide-exchange specialization and HSPA13 substrate-region divergence further limit a single family-wide activity description. Compartmental divergence is important but is not the only functional difference. No replacement family-wide ATPase grant is made.

subfamilies.label: Cytosolic/nuclear HSC70-HSP70 branch
subfamilies.description: The constitutive (HSC70/HSPA8) and stress-inducible (HSP70/HSPA1A-B, yeast SSA1-4) cytosolic chaperones. Core compartment is the cytosol, with stress-induced nuclear/nucleolar accumulation; members end in the GPTIEEVD motif that docks HOP/CHIP-type TPR co-chaperones. Cell-surface and exosomal pools are documented for several members but are context-specific moonlighting locations, not the evolved compartment -- and the current PAINT slice carries no plasma-membrane IBD anywhere in this family (see term_assessments).

subfamilies.label: ER-lumenal BiP/GRP78 branch
subfamilies.description: The endoplasmic reticulum HSP70 (BiP/GRP78/Kar2). A cleaved N-terminal signal peptide directs ER entry and a C-terminal KDEL (fungal HDEL) retrieval signal maintains steady-state lumenal residency (see the kdel_retention site). BiP is a soluble lumenal protein with no membrane-spanning segment; its membrane contact is peripheral (translocon-associated during co- and post-translational import, plus UPR-sensor complexes), which is why generic "membrane" reads as a granularity mismatch at gene level even though the branch node carrying it is correctly placed.

subfamilies.label: CHAPERONE PROTEIN HSCA
subfamilies.description: HscA (Hsc66) is the specialized Isc-system Hsp70-related ATPase partnered with HscB. E. coli HscA recognizes IscU and couples its nucleotide cycle to cluster transfer. IscU is its characterized physiological client, while in vitro antiaggregation assays also use model proteins. E. coli HscA P0A6Z1 is classified in PANTHER19 SF176; PSEPK Q88PK4 is kept in the separate family-level entry because no corresponding subfamily placement has been established. subfamilies.divergence_description: The supported specialization is ATP-dependent IscU cluster transfer and conformational-state selection. PMID22782893 shows stabilization of disordered IscU, and PMID9852006 demonstrates antiaggregation activity on model substrates. ATP hydrolysis, holdase behavior and client capture do not by themselves establish ATP-driven folding to a native state. This leaves the generic folding assignment unresolved rather than proving its loss or justifying a negative HscA exception. It also avoids transferring general heat-response or broad-client refolding claims solely from Hsp70 membership.

Stress-induced nuclear and nucleolar accumulation of cytosolic HSC70/HSP70 is a conserved, repeatedly observed behavior of this branch, with experimental seeds in both fungi and metazoa. The residual issue is that bare "membrane" is uninformative for a soluble ER-lumenal KDEL protein (see kdel_retention) whose membrane contact is peripheral and translocon-associated; the informative descendants (GO:0005789 ER membrane, GO:0005788 ER lumen) already exist on the affected genes. This is the informative localization for the BiP branch and the one the kdel_retention site mechanistically underwrites: signal-peptide-directed ER entry plus KDEL/HDEL receptor retrieval keeps these chaperones lumenal at steady state. Seeds span metazoa, budding and fission yeast, and the placement at the eukaryote-level BiP clade node matches the paralog's origin. Recorded alongside the GO:0016020 assessment because the contrast is the point: the same correctly placed node carries both the precise term and the uninformative parent.

PTN001065099 is not the ribosome-associated branch alone. Its 57 members span all of the fungal cytosolic Hsp70 subfamilies: the SSA chaperones (SF395 with S. cerevisiae SSA1/SSA2, S. pombe ssa1/ssa2, Neurospora hsps-1; SF385 with SSA3/SSA4), the ribosome-associated SSB group (SF467: SSB1/SSB2, S. pombe sks2), the RAC subunit SSZ1 (SF539) and a small LHS1-like group (SF522). On the same date the node was given an IBA for the broader GO:0006457 protein folding. For the SSB and SSZ1 branches the pruning is defensible. Their established role is folding nascent chains on the translating ribosome (Ssb at the ribosome-nascent chain complex, Ssz1 with zuotin in RAC), and none of them carries experimental evidence for refolding denatured or aggregated proteins. Our SSB1/SSB2/SSZ1 gene reviews already MODIFY the IBA to protein folding. For the SSA branch the loss is contradicted. S. cerevisiae SSA1 is itself one of the experimental seeds of the ancestral refolding IBD at PTN000452648 (SGD:S000000004), and it has two SGD IDA annotations for protein refolding: reactivation of chemically denatured luciferase by purified Ssa1 and its mutants (PMID:18706386), and reactivation of aggregated proteins together with Hsp104 and Hsp40 (PMID:9674429). Both are abstract-only in our cache, so we defer to the SGD curators who read the full text. Refolding by the Hsp70-Hsp40(-Hsp104) system is the core biochemistry of the cytosolic SSA paralogs and is shared with the metazoan HSC70/HSP70 seeds, so no divergence places the SSA clade outside the function. The IRD should therefore move from PTN001065099 to the node(s) above SSB (SF467) and SSZ1 (SF539), or be removed, and the SSA subfamilies (SF395, SF385) should again inherit GO:0042026. SF522 (LHS1-like) was not assessed. The affected subfamilies listed below are the ones for which the loss looks correct.

residue_sites.label: C-terminal KDEL/HDEL ER-retrieval signal
residue_sites.description: The C-terminal tetrapeptide of the BiP branch, bound in the Golgi by KDEL receptors that retrieve escaped lumenal proteins back to the ER. It is the sequence-level discriminator between the ER branch and the cytosolic branch in this family: BiP orthologs end in KDEL (fungal Kar2-type members in HDEL), while cytosolic HSC70/HSP70 members instead end in GPTIEEVD (verified for P63018 and P11142, both 646 aa ending ...GASSGPTIEEVD), the docking motif for TPR co-chaperones. A machine-checkable negative control is deliberately not encoded: the cytosolic EEVD terminus shares D and E with KDEL, so no single C-terminal position discriminates the two motifs at one-residue granularity.

residues.role: retrieval-signal position 1 (K in metazoan/plant BiP; H in the fungal HDEL variant)

required_for.rationale: KDEL-receptor retrieval maintains steady-state ER-lumenal residency of soluble chaperones that would otherwise leak into the secretory pathway. CONTRIBUTES rather than REQUIRED: ER entry and initial lumenal localization are directed by the cleaved N-terminal signal peptide and do not depend on the retrieval signal, whose loss causes slow secretion rather than absence from the lumen.

term_assessments.scope_reason: Recorded here because the disputed assertion no longer exists as a PAINT node/term pair to assess: no IBD for GO:0005886 survives anywhere in the current PTHR19375 slice (rows dated through 2026-08-28). The GOA WITH/FROM of rat Hspa8's plasma-membrane IBA names PTN002500132, which now carries only cytosol (GO:0005829) and nucleus (GO:0005634) -- PAINT has withdrawn or re-scoped the ancestral plasma-membrane claim, confirming the gene-side over-annotation calls (rat Hspa8 MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED; yeast SSA1-4/SSB2 REMOVE of the corresponding IBA). No phylogenetic propagation of this term is licensed in this family. The scope is UNRESOLVED rather than NOT_APPLICABLE deliberately: several members carry direct experimental evidence (HDA/TAS/IDA) of context-specific cell-surface and exosomal HSP70 pools -- human HSPA8 for one -- so a family-wide denial would be false. Surface localization is a member-by-member, condition-specific moonlighting observation that gene reviews may retain on direct evidence; it is not an inherited compartment.

The IBD behind the disputed rat Hspa5 IBA sits at the BiP-specific node PTN001834223 and is assessed SOUND above -- placement is not the problem. The gene-side objection is granularity: for a soluble ER-lumenal KDEL protein the bare "membrane" term adds nothing over ER membrane (GO:0005789) and the accepted ER-lumen annotations, which is a defect of the chosen term, not of the phylogeny. The scope axis here cannot express "correctly placed but uninformative", so this is deliberately UNRESOLVED rather than a grant or denial: peripheral membrane association is real across the BiP branch (and membrane-fraction HDA data exist for cytosolic members too), so no branch can be excluded as factually wrong, while endorsing the term family-wide would repeat the granularity mistake. The actionable family-level recommendation is that PAINT replace GO:0016020 at PTN001834223 with GO:0005789 (endoplasmic reticulum membrane) or drop it in favor of the co-located GO:0005788 IBD.

Canonical Hsp70/DnaK folding activity remains positive, including direct denatured-luciferase reactivation evidence for yeast Ssa1. A universal grant across this heterogeneous family is not justified. The current term requires ATP-driven assistance to protein folding; HscA ATPase stimulation, client capture and cluster transfer do not alone establish that endpoint. E. coli HscA stabilizes disordered IscU and has model-client antiaggregation activity, leaving generic folding uncertain rather than demonstrably absent. The negative Hsp110 judgment for HSPH1/Q92598 remains: it acts as a nucleotide-exchange factor and holdase rather than an independent ATP-driven folding chaperone. The exact former exception object is archived because live member exceptions cannot qualify an UNRESOLVED universal scope; no negative HscA exception, loss event or new broad ATPase grant is added. HSPA13 and other divergent proteins remain member-level questions.

Follow-up (2026-11-07): GO0140662 universal scope is now UNRESOLVED while canonical Hsp70 positives and the existing negative Hsp110 biological judgment are retained. This supersedes the family-wide activity interpretation in the historical completion note below. HscA uncertainty is not a demonstrated loss and does not alter any existing PAINT verdict, localization judgment, residue site, member identity or seed. No family-wide ATPase assessment was added. Completion (2026-10-24): every node/term pair in the current PTHR19375-paint.tsv slice now has a node assessment; bacterial DnaK and HscA branches were added so the family review covers the HscA representatives of the bacterial Isc iron-sulfur cluster assembly module, and GO:0140662 is assessed family-wide with an Hsp110 exception. The module grounds its HscA role to subfamily SF176 (CHAPERONE PROTEIN HSCA), where PANTHER 19.0 classifies E. coli HscA, rather than to the whole family, which also contains DnaK and the eukaryotic Hsp70s. Unlike the branches described in the original notes below, the HscA branch therefore carries an SF id, even though the UniProt cross-references and entries.csv still give only the family.
Original scope: this review adjudicates the two localization assertions disputed by the rat gene reviews -- Hspa8 GO:0005886 (plasma membrane, IBA from PTN002500132) and Hspa5 GO:0016020 (membrane, IBA from PTN001834223) -- in the context of the family's branch-wise localization structure.
Why the plasma-membrane adjudication is a term_assessment and not a node_assessment: the family validator checks every node_assessment against the cached PTHR19375-paint.tsv and fails any node/term pair PAINT does not currently record. GO:0005886 appears at no node in the current slice, so the withdrawn assertion is recorded as a term assessment, with the surviving content of PTN002500132 (cytosol, nucleus) assessed as node assessments instead.
Subfamily SF accessions are deliberately omitted: PANTHER classifies the cited members at family level only (their UniProt DR PANTHER cross-references carry no SF, and the subfamily column of PTHR19375-entries.csv is empty), so no SF id could be established for the branches. The branches are anchored to the PAINT clade nodes the IBDs actually sit on (PTN002500132, PTN001834223, PTN000452554), which is the axis the disputes are about.
Residue verification provenance: C-termini were read from UniProt REST on 2026-08-31 -- P06761 (654 aa, sv1) ends ...KDEL (651-654); P11021 (654 aa, sv2) ends ...KDEL (K651); P16474 (682 aa, sv1) ends ...HDEL (H679); P63018 and P11142 (both 646 aa) end ...GASSGPTIEEVD (no retrieval signal). family_name matches panther.obo verbatim; all representative members were confirmed present in PTHR19375-entries.csv. The live field was removed only because exceptions are legal on FAMILY_WIDE or SUBFAMILY_ONLY grants, not on UNRESOLVED scope. Its unchanged rationale is: Hsp110 proteins act as nucleotide exchange factors and holdases for canonical Hsp70s rather than as ATP-driven folding chaperones in their own right; PAINT places adenyl-nucleotide exchange factor activity on the Hsp110 branch.
